en.title: Kyle Chandler on Lanterns Finale: Hal and Halogram Were 'Never Fully Separated'
en.summary: Kyle Chandler, who plays Hal Jordan and his digital echo Halogram in HBO's Lanterns, reveals a profound connection between the two iterations of the character. The actor delved into the nuances of his final scene with John Stewart, offering a unique perspective on Halogram's development.
en.body:
The season one finale of HBO's **Lanterns** delivered a poignant conclusion for the relationship between John Stewart, played by **Aaron Pierre**, and Halogram, the digital recreation of Hal Jordan embodied by **Kyle Chandler**. While Halogram exists as a version of Hal Jordan from two decades prior, **Chandler** explained that the distinction between the original and the echo was far less defined than it might appear.

"Hal and Halogram were never fully separated; he [Halogram] is his [Hal’s] subconscious," **Chandler** stated at a recent press conference attended by Reactor Mag. This perspective sheds new light on Halogram’s journey throughout the season, particularly his evolving dynamic with John Stewart. **Chandler** sees Halogram’s experiences with John as integral to his own understanding, allowing him to finally process aspects of his past that the original Hal Jordan could not.

## The Mind of Hal Jordan

**Chandler** elaborated on his approach to the season’s final scene, emphasizing the continuous nature of Hal’s consciousness. "At that point, I think it’s Hal as a young man going through all those experiences and then finally learning in the end what it’s all about," he said. He highlighted how **Halogram**, through his interactions with **John Stewart**, gained a unique capacity for emotional expression and self-discovery that was previously inaccessible to him. "He could never pluck that string as Hal in the show, but as Halogram, he learned with Hal and he could pluck the string." The actor also praised the writing for Halogram’s final moments, calling the trick that led John to say "I love you" "just brilliant."

## A Father-Son Echo

The deep connection forged between John Stewart and Halogram in the latter half of the season has resonated with viewers, drawing parallels to a father-son dynamic. **Chandler**'s insight that Halogram is essentially Hal’s subconscious provides a compelling explanation for this perceived bond. It suggests that John wasn't just interacting with a digital archive of memories, but with a part of Hal's very being, grappling with unresolved emotions and experiences. This layered understanding of the character’s portrayal deepens the emotional impact of their final scenes together, offering a sophisticated exploration of identity and legacy within the superhero genre.

## What's Next

Details regarding the second season of **Lanterns** have not yet been announced, but **Kyle Chandler**'s reflections offer a rich foundation for future narrative explorations of the **Lanterns** mythology and the complex psyche of Hal Jordan.

The last few episodes of HBO’s Lanterns see Aaron Pierre’s John Stewart and Kyle Chandler’s Halogram become closer, with a father-son-type relationship that ends with a poignant moment near the end of the season finale . In a press conference Reactor attended after the season finale, Chandler explained that the relationship John developed with Halogram isn’t distinct from John’s relationship with the flesh-and-blood Hal, even though by 2026, Halogram is a version of Hal that’s 20 years out of date. For Chandler, Hal and Halogram “were never fully separated; he [Halogram] is his [Hal’s] subconscious. So there’s a lot to play with there.” Chandler brought up this interconnectedness between the two versions of Hal when describing how he approached the final scene he shares with Pierre. “At that point, I think it’s Hal as a young man going through all those experiences and then finally learning in the end what it’s all about,” he said, referencing Halogram’s journey with John over the last episodes of the season. “He could never pluck that string as Hal in the show, but as Halogram, he learned with Hal and he could pluck the string.” Chandler also added that he thought that Halogram tricking John into saying “I love you” was “just brilliant” writing, and that the scene overall hit home when he recently watched it. “It’s like when you win the state championship, tears come to your eyes because all the work that you put in slams into you at one moment on the field,” he said. “It happened to me this morning watching [Halogram] saying goodbye to him and the whole thing, and all that really did come packed into just a little shooting star, and I did have to gently wipe away a tear so my wife didn’t make fun of me.” You can (re)watch that shooting star moment yourself: the first season of Lanterns is now streaming on HBO Max.
